# Almost-simple groups generated by one actual Cartan component

For supplied integral component coordinates on an affine pinned model, assume
one algebraically closed field fibre is semisimple. The actual closed normal
semisimple subgroup generated by any one nonempty Cartan component is almost
simple. The module chooses such a group using the previously constructed
RootPartitionNormalModel and proves the result for every supplied model of that
component. No simple-connectedness or adjointness hypothesis is used.

The proof first shows that a nontrivial smooth connected closed normal subgroup
of a semisimple group contains some full root group. Otherwise the normal-root
dichotomy and root generation make it central; semisimplicity and commutativity
would make it trivial. For an internal normal subgroup of a component group,
the published normality-transfer theorem makes its composite normal in the
ambient group. A contained ambient root must belong to the selected component:
otherwise complement centrality and coroot containment would force its diagonal
Cartan pairing 2 to vanish. Normal root support is a union of Cartan components,
so every selected root group is contained. The retained root-generated
minimality then makes the internal subgroup the whole component group.
Nontriviality follows from a nonidentity actual root point in that component.

This is an internally derived field construction from the imported root-group,
normality-transfer, coroot and Cartan-support results. It prepares the affine
local-product route motivated by Conrad, *Reductive group schemes* (2014),
Proposition 6.4.4, pp.232–233. It does not assert an affine component product or
identify these field groups with relative derived centralizers.
